researched_writeups.title: Alibaba: The Only Non-US Stock in My Children's Portfolio — And Why Mr. Market Is Wrong Again
researched_writeups.summary: Evaluates Alibaba as a multi-year compounder trading at an unjustified low-teens earnings multiple ($117 per share vs $268B market cap) following short-term earnings pressure. Argues that Wall Street is penalizing temporary margin compression caused by heavy reinvestment into AI and cloud infrastructure, while core asset-light marketplaces (Taobao/Tmall) remain highly cash-generative. Identifies accelerating cloud growth (reaching 40%) and Apple's selection of Alibaba's Qwen LLM for Apple Intelligence in China as key catalysts for fundamental re-rating.

researched_writeups.title: Investment thesis on Alibaba Group
researched_writeups.summary: Analyzes Alibaba as a deep value opportunity relative to its market power in Chinese e-commerce and cloud infrastructure, generating RMB 79.7 billion in net income in FY2024. Constructs a conservative Discounted Cash Flow model under pessimistic macro assumptions, yielding a baseline intrinsic valuation of $121.24 per share to provide a substantial margin of safety. Points to government stimulus targeting domestic consumption, growth in cross-border e-commerce (AIDC), and AI-driven cloud enterprise adoption as operational catalysts.

researched_writeups.title: In depth review of Alibaba (BABA)
researched_writeups.summary: Presents a segment-level due diligence memo examining the valuation dislocation between Alibaba's strong operational cash flow generation and depressed valuation multiples driven by regulatory and geopolitical fear. Evaluates unit economics across Taobao/Tmall, Cainiao logistics, and Cloud Intelligence, demonstrating that core domestic retail cash flow adequately funds growth initiatives and buybacks. Cites shifting Chinese government support toward tech innovation, domestic consumption stimulus, and stabilization in real estate sentiment as catalysts for multiple expansion.

researched_writeups.title: Oakmark International Fund: Third Calendar Quarter 2024 Commentary
researched_writeups.summary: Details Oakmark's high-conviction value thesis on Alibaba following macroeconomic policy support in China. Maintains that public markets fail to appreciate the operational turnaround occurring across core Taobao and Tmall e-commerce properties, as well as the unpriced asset value within Alibaba Cloud and international logistics. Reaffirms that Alibaba trades at a substantial discount to normalized free cash flow yield relative to global peer tech platforms.
